title: Vision failure modes
summary: Vision models read images fluently but wrongly in predictable places: counting, spatial positions, small or rotated text, chart details and metadata. Know the list, route around it and test each failure class.
useIf: You rely on a vision model for answers that people will act on, and you need a plan for the known weak spots.
avoidIf: The task is coarse description where an occasional miss is harmless. Heavy mitigation would cost more than the error.

explain.md: A vision model does not measure an image. It produces a plausible reading, so errors look as confident as correct answers. OpenAI's guide lists the known weak spots (checked 2026-10-13) [[r1]]: specialised medical images such as CT scans are unsuitable; non-Latin text such as Japanese or Korean may degrade; **small text** needs enlarging or `detail: original`; **rotated** or upside-down content is misread; graphs where line style or colour varies are hard; **precise spatial localisation** (a chess position) fails; descriptions can be wrong; panoramic and fisheye shapes struggle; **counts are approximate**; file names and metadata are not processed, and images may be resized even at `original`; CAPTCHAs are blocked.

The fix is rarely a better prompt. It is a different representation: crop and enlarge for small text, extract characters with a layout service, ask for a chart's underlying data table and compute in code, count per region and reconcile, and pass metadata as text. Then measure each failure class on its own.

explain.title: Route around a known weak spot
explain.alt: An image is preprocessed, routed to OCR, a detector or a data-table step, verified, and sent to human review when confidence is low.

flowchart LR
  I[Image] --> P[Crop, deskew, enlarge]

  R -->|Counts| C[Count per crop]
  R -->|Chart| T[Data table]
  O --> V[Verify]
  C --> V
  T --> V
  V --> H[Human review if low confidence]

explain.title: Test by stratum
explain.md: A golden set that mixes easy and hard images hides these failures. Tag each image by class (small text, rotated, chart, count) and report accuracy per class.

pitfalls.cause: The model returned approximate counts and nobody reconciled them
pitfalls.fix: Count per region, sum, set a tolerance and sample-check against a manual count.

pitfalls.symptom: Chart answers quote the wrong series
pitfalls.cause: Varying line styles and colours are hard for the model
pitfalls.fix: Ask for the data table first, validate it, and compute the answer in code.

pitfalls.symptom: Quality is fine in tests and poor in production
pitfalls.cause: Test images were clean and upright, while real ones were rotated or low resolution
pitfalls.fix: Build the golden set from real uploads, tagged by failure class.

scenarios.title: Counting items on shelves
scenarios.situation: A retailer wants stock levels from shelf photos. A wrong count triggers a reorder or a missed one. Photos are wide shots taken on phones.
constraints: Counts are approximate in the model
unknowns: Is a manual spot check possible?
scenarios.question: How do you produce the count?

options.name: Count per cropped shelf region, sum, and sample-check against manual counts
options.why: It works around approximate counting by shrinking each count and measuring error.
options.tradeoff: More calls, and you must define regions.

options.name: A structured detector for the product classes
options.why: Detectors return explicit boxes you can count and audit.
options.tradeoff: You train and maintain it per catalogue.

options.name: Ask the vision model for the total in one prompt
options.why: The documented limit says counts may be approximate, and the error is invisible.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable for a rough 'about how many' display with no financial consequence.

flips.if: Shelves are rigid and cameras are fixed
flips.then: A detector or fixed-region counting becomes cheap and accurate.
A direct vision call is enough.

scenarios.takeaway: Exact numbers need decomposition and measurement, not a bigger prompt.

scenarios.title: Rotated scans in Japanese
scenarios.situation: A back office receives phone scans of paper forms in Japanese. Some are rotated or upside down, and the text is small. Wrong characters flow into a database.
unknowns: Does the OCR service support the languages?
What share of scans are rotated?
scenarios.question: What is the pipeline?

options.name: Deskew and rotate, run layout extraction with language support, then reason over the text with confidence checks
options.why: Targets all three documented weak spots (non-Latin, small text, rotation) with a purpose-built reader [[r1]] [[r10]].
options.tradeoff: More components, and you must verify language support.

options.name: Vision model at `original` detail on the raw scan
options.why: Helps small text and needs one call.
options.tradeoff: Rotation and non-Latin text remain weak spots and there is no confidence score.

options.name: Vision model at `low` detail
options.why: Discards the small characters you need.
options.tradeoff: Fine only to classify the document type first.

flips.if: Volume is a few dozen forms a week
flips.then: Use `original` and a human check instead of building extraction.
Use a prebuilt form model in the extraction step.

scenarios.takeaway: Stack the right reader under the model when several weak spots overlap.

quiz.q: A model reports 47 items on a shelf and a manual count says 52. Which design change addresses the cause?
options: Count per cropped region and reconcile
Ask the same question three times and average
quiz.explain: Approximate counting is a documented limit, so decompose the task and measure. Temperature does not add precision, `low` removes detail, and averaging repeats the same bias.

quiz.q: Which items are documented limitations of OpenAI vision models on 2026-10-13?
options: Small text may be misread unless enlarged
File names and metadata are not processed
Images are never resized at `original` detail
Rotated or upside-down content may be misread
quiz.explain: Small text, metadata and rotation are listed. The guide says images may still be resized at `original`, so option three is false.

quiz.q: Match each failure class to the better route.

pairs.r: Request a data table, compute in code

quiz.explain: Each route replaces a description with a measurable representation.

flashcards.front: Name four documented weak spots of vision models.
flashcards.back: Small text, rotated content, approximate counts, precise spatial localisation. Also non-Latin text, varied-style graphs, panoramic images and ignored metadata.

flashcards.front: How do you handle chart questions that need exact numbers?
flashcards.back: Ask for the underlying data table, validate it, and compute the answer in code instead of reading a value off the picture.

flashcards.front: Why test vision features by stratum?
flashcards.back: A mixed golden set hides class-specific failures. Tag images by small text, rotation, chart or count and report accuracy for each.
